title: ImprovEvolve: Ask AlphaEvolve to Improve the Input Solution and Then Improvise

mechanism.domainTask: Evolving modular initialization, local-improvement, and perturbation code for challenging continuous/global optimization problems
mechanism.populationDetail: Outer candidate optimizer programs are maintained in a single-island GigaEvo MAP-Elites population/archive; no multi-island or tree structure is used.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The adopted GigaEvo setup uses MAP-Elites with fitness as a single descriptor discretized into 150 bins.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The outer archive is inherited from GigaEvo; inner solution states in basin-hopping are not the evolutionary population of candidate programs.
mechanism.generationDetail: The outer LLM produces a mutated offspring program from two selected parent programs, but the paper does not specify whether both are fused or one is the primary editable base and the other context.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The GigaEvo context pipeline and parent-associated metrics are inherited infrastructure, not a new feedback module proposed by ImprovEvolve.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Six elites are first sampled from the archive proportional to fitness; two parent programs are then sampled uniformly from that elite set.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The evolved candidate is a modular optimizer program whose evaluation executes a nested basin-hopping procedure over problem solutions, separating optimizer-program evolution from solution-space optimization.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/ImprovEvolve Ask AlphaEvolve to Improve the Input Solution and Then Improvise.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Survey currently cites ImprovEvolve as a QD and parent-selection example. Those outer-loop mechanisms are inherited from GigaEvo. The explicit fixed exploration/refinement schedule is inside candidate execution (basin-hopping), not the outer LLM operator selector. The relationship between two selected parent programs and offspring is not specified enough to assign multi-parent fusion.
